transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-16
Time: 14:30 UTC (06:30 PT)
Duration: ~42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood, AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood, SE), Jordan Lee (ClearPath, CTO), Maya Patel (ClearPath, Head of ML), Sam Rivera (ClearPath, SRE)

Summary:
Quick walkthrough of Redwood's model catalog and how ClearPath can pick open models for their triage and clinical note summarization workloads. Discussed benchmarks, hardware compatibility (A100/H100/CPU), quantization tradeoffs, and next steps for a pilot run.

Topics:
- Model catalog UI and API filters
- Benchmarks and compatibility matrix (latency/cost/accuracy)
- Quantization profiles and accuracy tradeoffs
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) deployment options
- Next steps: share docs, schedule pilot, pricing

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll give a quick tour of the model catalog and then Priya will run through compatibility and benchmarks. how's that sound?
[00:08] Jordan Lee: sounds good, Alex, thanks. we have about 40 minutes. Maya and Sam are on in case we dive into infra.
[00:15] Maya Patel: yep hi, excited to see the model selection flow.
[00:18] Priya Natarajan: great, i'll share my screen in a sec, just flagging some parts may show model names that are a bit mangled in the transcript, sorry in advance for any typos.
[00:27] Sam Rivera: no worries. our main goals: lower latency for triage, keep costs reasonable, and ensure PHI never leaves our VPC if possible.
[00:37] Alex Chen: perfect, that's exactly what we'll focus on. quick context — Redwood's model catalog lets you filter by task (summarization, chat, embeddings), by hardware compatibility, and by verified benchmarks — latency, cost tokens, and eval metrics.
[00:52] Priya Natarajan: okay sharing screen — you should see the catalog UI. top left there are filters for model family, sequence length profile, supported hardware (A100, H100, CPU quantized), and whether the model has Redwood-verified benchmarks.
[01:12] Jordan Lee: can you show an example for a summarization model we'd use for notes?
[01:18] Priya Natarajan: sure, search for "summarization" then filter for sequence length ~1k and hardware H100. you'll see several open models we recommend — some 7B and 13B variants, and a few 30B that are optimized/quantized. note the catalog also includes a compatibility matrix link for each model.
[01:36] Maya Patel: what's the accuracy delta when you quantize a 13B model to 4-bit? we saw a lot of variability in other stacks.
[01:44] Priya Natarajan: good question. our compatibility matrix includes eval rows — for a typical clinical summarization eval set we run standard rouge/med-bleu-ish metrics, and for many 13B models 4-bit PTQ shows <2-3% drop in F1 vs fp16 on average but it depends on the model. we surface recommended quant profiles per model.
[02:07] Sam Rivera: and the catalog shows the expected token latency? is that averaged on A100 or H100?
[02:13] Priya Natarajan: by default the benchmark numbers are labeled — we run both A100 and H100, and also provide a CPU baseline for small models. the latency shown is median p50 per-token at a 512-context with batching=1 unless otherwise noted. we also include throughput with batching configs.
[02:30] Alex Chen: i'd call out that for production you can pin a model version and we store per-route metrics in the console so you can compare real traffic to our benchmark numbers.
[02:38] Jordan Lee: for privacy we're likely looking at private deployment (VPC) or on-prem. how different are the numbers in private vs hosted?
[02:46] Priya Natarajan: performance is mostly runtime-dependent. the same runtime runs in hosted and private. the differences come down to the underlying GPU and kernel availability — e.g., a dedicated H100 cluster will match or exceed hosted H100 latencies. our compatibility matrix indicates which kernels are required; sometimes we use fused attention kernels that are vendor-specific and we note that in the model page.
[03:03] Maya Patel: can you point to a specific model page?
[03:07] Priya Natarajan: clicking into the 13B-sum-proto entry — you'll see tabs: Overview, Benchmarks, Compatibility, Deployments. Benchmarks has latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens estimate. Compatibility shows kernel support (triton/cuDNN/custom), supported sequence lengths, KV cache behavior, and whether the model plays well with dynamic batching.
[03:33] Jordan Lee: kernel support — are you referencing Triton or something proprietary?
[03:37] Priya Natarajan: primarily Triton + custom kernels. we compile and select kernels at deploy time; the matrix says e.g. "requires fused-attn-v2" or "works with standard attention". if a target infra doesn't support the fused kernel we recommend the alternative model variant or a different quant profile.
[03:52] Sam Rivera: for VPC, what about KMS/HSM and audit logs — do you have SOC2 stuff?
[03:57] Alex Chen: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II, SAML/SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations; for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and HSM. we'll share the security pack.
[04:07] Jordan Lee: great. curious about cost math — is the cost/tokens in the UI across a mix of batch sizes?
[04:14] Priya Natarajan: cost estimate shows the default serving profile — batch size tuned for 99th percentile latency SLO. we also provide a "cost/throughput" knob where you can view cost per effective token under higher batching assumptions. Optimize gives suggestions — for example, swap to a 7B quantized model for non-critical summarization, or enable KV prefix caching for repeated patient-note prefixes to save tokens.
[04:40] Maya Patel: prefix caching — is that automatic or do we need to change prompts?
[04:44] Priya Natarajan: automatic if you configure the route to enable prefix/KV caching and provide a cache key (we have SDK helpers). for example if the first ~200 tokens are static demographic/context we can cache the KV and reduce compute on subsequent calls.
[04:57] Jordan Lee: any out-of-the-box evals we can run? we want to avoid building too much infra for the pilot.
[05:03] Alex Chen: yes, we have evaluation harnesses — you can upload your prompt set and reference summaries and we can run a bench on our infra, or we can run it in your VPC if you need private. results show both latency and accuracy metrics and we store the eval so you can track regressions.
[05:20] Priya Natarajan: demoing now the Benchmarks tab — here's p50/p95, token cost; clicking the compatibility matrix shows hardware rows (A100, H100, T4, CPU) and columns for quant profiles (fp16, int8, 4-bit). cells have notes like "works, minor repro artifacts" or "not recommended".
[05:40] Jordan Lee: when you say int8 do you mean native int8 kernels or simulated? we've seen simulated int8 that loses more quality.
[05:46] Priya Natarajan: good call — we label simulated vs native. native int8 means kernel and runtime support, simulated indicates we did an emulation for quick cost estimates. for pilot we recommend native-supported paths.
[05:58] Sam Rivera: network-wise, if we run private in our GCP project what's the egress pattern to Redwood?
[06:04] Alex Chen: for Private you control the control plane connection. we can do a customer-managed control plane where logs and metrics are pushed to your ELK/stack, or a private link. detailed network diagram in the security pack we'll send.
[06:17] Maya Patel: question on model drift and rollouts — can we do canary & A/B?
[06:22] Priya Natarajan: yes console supports rollouts: split traffic, compare eval metrics per route, and automatic fallback if latency exceeds threshold. Optimize can propose a fallback model variant if quality drop is detected.
[06:35] Jordan Lee: are there examples of customers who moved from hosted to dedicated to private? curious about the migration path.
[06:41] Alex Chen: yes, many customers start hosted for quick iteration then move to Dedicated (reserved capacity) as throughput needs and SLAs mature, and then Private for regulatory needs. we can share case studies.
[06:52] Priya Natarajan: going back to the model page, under "Deployments" we show supported deployment modes. it also lists recommended GPU types and expected rack density. for example the 30B quantized variant needs 80GB GPU memory or sharded execution across 2x80GB.
[07:10] Maya Patel: that's helpful. do you have an API endpoint to query the catalog programmatically? we want to automate model selection in our CI.
[07:16] Alex Chen: yes there's a Catalog API — GET /models returns metadata, benchmarks, compatibility flags, and recommended quant profile. you can pin model versions via API too.
[07:27] Jordan Lee: for the pilot we plan to test a 13B quantized model and a 7B fp16 baseline; can you summarize what you'd need from us?
[07:34] Priya Natarajan: ideal: (1) sample prompt set and reference summaries, (2) traffic profile (qps, avg tokens), (3) preferred infra (H100/cloud project) and whether you'll want hosted vs private. with that we can run accuracy+latency bench and propose serving profile.
[07:48] Sam Rivera: we can provide a sanitized subset of notes and an infra contact.
[07:52] Alex Chen: great. quick demo note — the Console has a "Run Bench" button that will spin up the selected model in a sandbox and run your prompts; if you prefer we can run the bench in your VPC to avoid data egress.
[08:05] Jordan Lee: pricing — do you have ballpark TCO for dedicated H100 per month vs hosted usage?
[08:12] Alex Chen: we'll send a pricing sheet, but high level: hosted is pay-as-you-go with per-token and per-inference instance charges; dedicated is a reserved capacity discount with predictable throughput. for high volume H100 usage dedicated often reduces unit cost by 30-50% depending on commit. we'll include modeled scenarios.
[08:30] Maya Patel: regarding eval metrics — do you run clinical-specific metrics or do we need to provide eval code?
[08:36] Priya Natarajan: we have a generic eval harness (rouge, bleu, chrF) and a custom metric plug-in system; you can provide clinical metrics and we'll plug them in for the eval.
[08:48] Jordan Lee: any concerns about hallucinations in the summarization use case? we've seen models confidently state medications that aren't in the notes.
[08:55] Priya Natarajan: we recommend prompt engineering + fact-checking via retrieval or structured extraction steps. Optimize can suggest a two-step pipeline: extract structured fields then generate a summary constrained by the extracted facts. also you can run rerank/verify calls to an ensemble.
[09:14] Sam Rivera: from an ops perspective, what monitoring hooks do you provide?
[09:18] Alex Chen: per-route traces, token-level cost breakdown, error rates, latency histograms, and payload sampling for QA. you can export metrics to Prometheus and logs to your SIEM.
[09:29] Maya Patel: nice. one more on model compatibility — do you support adapters or LoRA style fine-tunes in the catalog?
[09:36] Priya Natarajan: catalog shows both base models and verified adapter/LoRA variants. we can host your fine-tuned artifacts as private model versions if needed.
[09:48] Jordan Lee: lovely. let's recap next steps.
[09:51] Alex Chen: recap: we'll share pricing + security pack; Priya will share the compatibility matrix and recommended quant profiles; you (Jordan/Maya) will send sample prompts and indicate infra preference. we'll schedule a pilot run targeted week of 2026-03-23.
[10:08] Maya Patel: sounds good.
[10:10] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[10:13] Alex Chen: thanks all — action items in the deck and i'll follow up in email.
[10:17] End of recording.
